name: Shadimetry for WooCommerce
author: exotomicdev

sections.description:
Shadimetry Free lets merchants configure a complete width × drop price matrix for a simple WooCommerce product. Customers enter finished measurements in cm. The server selects the first inclusive upper bands and uses that cell as the product’s base unit price.

Includes a native product editor, strict validation, server price preview, separate cart lines for different measurements, quantity handling, current-grid repricing and visible order item dimensions. All included functionality is unlocked, with no account, trial limit, tracking, external API or paid service.

Grid prices replace regular and sale prices. Saving a valid grid sets the product’s regular price to the lowest grid price and removes any sale price, so catalog sorting, price filters, feeds and search-engine structured data (published as a low–high price range) stay consistent with the grid. Coupons remain handled by WooCommerce. Grid prices follow the store’s normal inclusive/exclusive tax entry mode. The store owns currency, display tax and rounding. Decimal dimensions allow at most one decimal digit; no inches conversion is included.

Use the classic WooCommerce product editor and native simple-product form. Cart and Checkout blocks can process items added using that form. Direct Store API configured-product additions, newer interactive add-to-cart blocks, variations, bundles, composites and subscriptions are not supported. Requires 64-bit PHP.

Local tests covered WordPress 6.6 / PHP 8.1.34 / WooCommerce 9.3.3 with Twenty Twenty-Four 1.2, and WordPress 7.1.4 / PHP 8.5.12 / WooCommerce 11.2.1 with Twenty Twenty-Four 1.6 and Twenty Twenty-Five 1.5. Classic orders, HPOS, taxes, shipping and classic/Store API checkout were exercised. These exact combinations do not establish compatibility with every intervening release, extension or theme.

Known layout limitation: in the tested WooCommerce 11.2.1 themes, the Cart block can overflow narrow screens (320/375 px), including with Shadimetry deactivated. The classic cart fitted the tested 320, 375, 390 and 768 px viewports. Check your chosen theme and cart layout on staging. No global theme CSS override is included.

Keyboard navigation, focus, field labels and error recovery were checked in desktop browsers, with automated accessibility checks on the measurement form. Physical phones and screen readers have not been tested yet, and no WCAG conformance is claimed. No CSV import is included. Test the product, cart, taxes and checkout on a staging copy of your store before taking orders.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate WooCommerce.
  2. Install Shadimetry for WooCommerce from Plugins → Add Plugin, or upload the plugin ZIP, then activate it.
  3. Edit a simple product and open Product data → General.
  4. Enable Shadimetry, enter semicolon-separated bands and complete price rows, then save. The regular price is set to the lowest grid price.
  5. Test the product, cart, taxes and an offline checkout before store use.

See README.md for an illustrated text example and detailed rules.
sections.faq:
Which cart layout is recommended?

Use the native simple-product measurement form with the classic Cart and Checkout shortcodes. Assign those pages in WooCommerce settings and check all navigation links. In the tested current themes, the Cart block overflows narrow viewports even with Shadimetry deactivated. No global theme CSS fix is included.

What happens if the grid changes?

Every request reprices carts with the current grid. If the price changes while a shopper is already on the checkout page, the order is created at the current grid price, as WooCommerce does for a normal price change; Shadimetry only rejects a change detected within the checkout request itself. Avoid editing grids during busy trading hours. Invalid/removed grids or disabling custom pricing remove old configured cart lines. New purchases of a disabled product use the product’s regular price, which is the lowest price of its last saved grid.

Can I create orders for configured products in the admin?

Not yet. Orders created manually in the WooCommerce admin or through the REST API use the product’s regular price and contain no measurements. Have the customer order through the product page, or enter the line price and the measurements yourself.

Does it work with currency switchers, dynamic pricing or role-based pricing plugins?

Not supported. Plugins that change a configured product’s price after Shadimetry, or show prices in another currency, make the configured product impossible to order: checkout stops with a price-change error rather than charging an unchecked amount. Test any pricing extension on staging first.

Does “Order again” work?

Not for configured products. Reordering, and cart-recovery tools that re-add products without the measurement form, cannot add custom-size items; the customer must enter the measurements again on the product page.

Can I change store currency or precision?

Review and explicitly save each grid in the new currency/precision. Until then configured purchases fail validation. No automatic conversion occurs.

Does this import supplier spreadsheets?

No. This release provides manual grid entry only. A future add-on would be a separate plugin, without locking features in Free.

Are taxes calculated by Shadimetry?

No. Enter grid prices in the same tax mode as normal WooCommerce product prices. WooCommerce calculates and formats all taxes and totals.

Is anything sent to external services?

Shadimetry sends no outgoing requests and loads its own assets locally. Its same-origin price preview does not persist measurements. WooCommerce and other installed plugins retain their own behavior.

What data is retained after uninstall?

Saved product grids and historical order metadata remain to protect merchant pricing and order evidence. When switching from ShadeGrid, deactivate the old plugin before activating Shadimetry. Do not run both copies. Technical identifiers retain their historical shadegrid prefix; no data migration is required.
sections.changelog:
0.1.3

  • Scope coexistence checks to candidate activation; unrelated plugins remain manageable even when conflicting historical flags exist.
  • Rename the display name, package and text domain to Shadimetry for WooCommerce.
  • Preserve historical pricing grids, cart sessions, order metadata and financial calculations.
  • Prevent concurrent activation and pricing with another ShadeGrid or Shadimetry copy.

0.1.2

  • Saving a valid grid sets the regular price to the lowest grid price and clears sale prices, so catalog sorting, price filters and feeds no longer use an unrelated price.
  • Publish the grid’s low–high range as an AggregateOffer in product structured data.
  • Disable Shadimetry automatically when a product is changed to an unsupported type, instead of leaving a hidden enabled setting.
  • Show shoppers a neutral message instead of merchant configuration instructions.
  • Do not flag a measurement as invalid before the shopper has filled in both fields.
  • Document unsupported admin-created orders, pricing plugins, “Order again” and grid changes during checkout.

0.1.1

  • Reject a grid change detected within the checkout request instead of silently mutating the unit price.
  • Give every measurement form unique label and description targets.
  • Identify the invalid measurement without falsely flagging a valid field, and improve touch targets/focus.
  • Handle malformed saved editor values without a PHP error.
  • Preserve WooCommerce tax suffixes and dynamic amounts in catalog grid price ranges.
  • Exclude developer documentation and test files from the installation package.

0.1.0

  • Initial development version with server pricing, validation, classic and block checkout integration and HPOS-safe order metadata.
